info.name: Dalai Llama - Project Requirements
info.description: creative-planning-service's project-requirements flow (standalone brief -> duration/language pricing -> product + reference-material -> funding-triggered analysis), plus the billing-service video-pricing quote and brand-context endpoints it wires into. Set {{jwt}} and {{tenantId}} before running; {{requirementId}} and {{productId}} are set automatically by the 'Create standalone requirement' request's test script. This collection is meant to grow -- add one folder per controller, one request per endpoint, and attach a saved example response (Send, then 'Save as Example') so the next person can see a real request/response pair without having to run it first.

item.name: Create standalone requirement (multipart: brand, product, images)

request.description: Entry point B: no locked idea, no branding chat. `data` is CreateStandaloneRequirementRequest as JSON -- attach it as a text part with its own Content-Type set to application/json (Postman: click the part's row, use the dropdown on the right to pick 'Text', then set Content-Type via the part's header override, or just leave the default 'Text' type -- Spring's @RequestPart binds it as JSON either way since the body below already declares contentType). `brandContext` and `productDetails` are both optional -- set either to null (or drop the whole key) to skip upserting a brand / creating a product. `image` is the brief's own reference attachment; `productImages` (only used if productDetails is present) and `projectReferenceImages` ('what the client has in mind', unrelated to the product) are optional multi-file parts -- add more rows with the same key to attach more than one file. None of the three image sets are analyzed synchronously -- see 'Mark funded' below, which is what actually triggers analysis.

request.description: Tenant self-report of an out-of-band payment (see ProjectRequirementService's class javadoc -- never processes a payment itself). item.name: Lock chosen idea (creates the pre-production project)

request.description:
Idempotent end to end: calling this twice for the same requirement -- a double-click, a client retry after a dropped response -- always returns the SAME LockedIdea/project pair rather than minting a second project.

This used to be a real bug: the LockedIdea insert and the pre-production-service HTTP call lived in one @Transactional method, so a failure after pre-production-service had already committed its Project (a timeout, a blip) rolled the LockedIdea insert back too. A retry then found no existing LockedIdea, created a second one, and pre-production-service (having no idempotency guard of its own) created a second, orphaned Project -- same tenant, same idea title, two different statuses (e.g. DRAFT sitting next to SCRIPT_READY). Fixed on both sides: creative-planning-service now commits the LockedIdea row and the projectId attachment as two independent transactions (see LockedIdeaWriter) so a downstream failure can never undo the insert, and pre-production-service's POST /v1/projects/from-locked-idea is now idempotent by lockedIdeaId as defense in depth.

item.name: Edit brief (multipart: text, brand, product, images)

request.description: Lets whoever holds the link fill in the brief themselves -- every field independent and optional. `data.brand` upserts this tenant's one brand row; `data.product` updates the requirement's product if one exists, otherwise creates it (needs a brand to already exist, inline in the same request or from an earlier edit -- a blank product.name is silently skipped, not an error). `images` are project reference images ('what the client has in mind'); `productImages` attach to the product. Refused with 400 once `funded` is true.

response.name: 400 Bad Request -- already funded

item.name: Start payment (Razorpay order for the quoted price)

request.description: Charges exactly the already-quoted quotedTotalPrice -- no re-quoting. Returns paymentId/gatewayOrderId/amount/currency/keyId for the client to hand to Razorpay Checkout. This and /verify both call out to billing-service's live Razorpay integration with a 30s budget (BILLING_SERVICE_TIMEOUT_MS, bumped from 15s -- a real order-creation/verify call to Razorpay occasionally took longer than 15s, timing out the client-facing request even though billing-service's own call kept running and often still succeeded). Funding self-heals if /verify still times out: billing-service's real webhook independently publishes billing.payment.received once Razorpay confirms, and creative-planning-service's BillingEventConsumer applies the exact same funded transition from that event, idempotently, whichever arrives first.

item.name: Verify payment (funds the brief on success)

request.description: Verifies the Razorpay signature server-side (billing-service), then applies the same funding transition Mark funded / the Kafka billing.payment.received consumer does -- idempotent either way. This is the real client-callback path; Mark funded above is the tenant self-report / webhook-secret path.

response.name: 200 OK -- now funded

item.name: Client Review Page (pre-production-service, no auth)
item.description: pre-production-service's PublicProjectController, reached via /review/{{reviewToken}} in creator-ui. Set {{reviewToken}} from 'Get client review link' below (creator-authenticated) before running this folder.

item.name: Get the locked package (script, screenplay, cast, shots)

request.description: Calls billing-service's /client-review/verify (30s budget -- BILLING_SERVICE_TIMEOUT_MS) then locks the project. Unlike requirement funding, this had no async fallback until now: a timed-out verify left the project permanently unlocked even after a real charge, because nothing else was watching. Now self-heals the same way funding does, just without Kafka -- Razorpay's own payment.captured webhook hits billing-service directly, RazorpayWebhookOrchestrationService looks the order up in client_review_payment when it's not a wallet/funding Payment, marks it SUCCESS (idempotent, safe if this synchronous verify already did), and calls pre-production-service's new internal endpoint (POST /api/v1/internal/tenants/{tenantId}/projects/{projectId}/client-review-payment-captured, body {kind}) which locks the project or opens a paid extra review depending on client_review_payment.kind. Both target actions are already idempotent (relocking a CLIENT_LOCKED project is a no-op; starting a review returns the existing OPEN one), so it's harmless if this synchronous verify and the webhook both eventually succeed.

request.description: Only scriptText is required -- omitted narrative fields (logline, hook, etc.) fall back to the version being edited from, not blanked out. No LLM call; also updates the live script row so the edit actually takes effect on the next screenplay/shot generation.

item.name: Generate shot list (tags PRODUCT_HERO/MOTION_GRAPHIC, auto-plans motion graphics + lighting/camera)

request.description:
PRE_PROD_SHOT_LIST_GENERATE classifies every shot's shotType from the script + scene context (DIALOGUE/ACTION/PRODUCT_HERO/B_ROLL/TRANSITION/MOTION_GRAPHIC) -- PRODUCT_HERO shots also get a productShotType (Hero Shot/Ingredient Shot/Lifestyle Shot/Pack Shot). A MOTION_GRAPHIC shot has no camera plan and nothing for video-generation-service to dispatch to; instead, right after this call saves the shot list (and once that write has committed), ShotListController plans every MOTION_GRAPHIC shot via MotionGraphicPlanService, AND every other (camera-planned) shot via LightingPlanService + CameraPlanService -- all best-effort per shot/kind, so one LLM hiccup (or a failed critique retry) planning one shot's one plan never costs the shot list that just generated, or the rest of that shot's plans/images. GET a shot's plan below; the 'Plan'/'Replan' actions in the UI are now the manual fallback/revision path, not the only way to get one -- image generation for each of the 4 kinds (Storyboard/Production/Lighting/Camera plan) still stays a deliberate manual click per shot.

editingNotes and screenDirection (prompt v5) are written against the shot's actual neighbors, not in isolation -- editingNotes names the cut technique into this shot (J-cut, match cut, whip pan, etc), what continuity carries across it (screen direction, prop/costume state, eyeline), and the pacing rhythm relative to the surrounding shots. Before that, these two fields read as generic, interchangeable notes across shots.

item.name: Replan a shot's lighting (critique-and-retry, up to 2 attempts)

request.description: Now auto-generated for every camera-planned shot (everything except MOTION_GRAPHIC) right after shot-list generation -- see ShotListController/ShotListGenerationService#planLightingAndCameraForShots. This is the manual fallback/replan. Runs PRE_PROD_LIGHTING_PLAN_GENERATE, then PRE_PROD_LIGHTING_PLAN_CRITIC against the result; on FAIL, regenerates once more with the critic's issues fed back. source=CRITIC (with critiqueNotes) if a retry happened, else GENERATED. Also folds in the shot's ShotProductReference analysis (reference lighting style/mood/subject), when one exists, instead of planning from the shot's flat fields alone.

item.name: Edit a shot's lighting plan (manual correction, no LLM call)

request.description: Every field optional -- only what's sent changes, everything else keeps its current value. Sets source=EDITED and clears critiqueNotes.

item.name: Replan a shot's camera (critique-and-retry, up to 2 attempts)

request.description: Same auto-generation + critique-and-retry shape as the lighting plan above (PRE_PROD_CAMERA_PLAN_GENERATE -> PRE_PROD_CAMERA_PLAN_CRITIC), also folding in the shot's ShotProductReference analysis (reference camera angle/motion) when one exists.

request.description: Every field optional -- only what's sent changes, everything else keeps its current value. Sets source=EDITED and clears critiqueNotes.
